native_result.query: What proportion of studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in a lab setting?
native_result.HypoA: In Experimental Economics, all studies (both original and replication) were conducted in a lab setting (100%), while in Psychology, a small proportion of replication studies were also conducted online (8.8%)
native_result.HypoB: All 18 original Experimental Economics studies (`project == 'ee'`) were conducted in a lab setting: 18/18 = 100%, where 'lab setting' is operationalized as the original experiment not being online (`online.o == 0`), one row per unique original study (18 rows = 18 unique `id` = 18 unique `title`, no duplicate O/R pairs), denominator = ee studies with non-missing `online.o` (none missing). 'Lab' is proxied because no direct lab field is populated for ee (`lab_id` is NA for all 18), but four independently coded setting markers converge on the same 18 studies: `online.o == 0`, `subjects.o` in {students, community}, `compensation.o == 'cash'`, and non-missing `experiment_country.o`. Caveat reported explicitly: `online.o` is degenerate within ee (all 18 are 0), so numerator equals denominator by construction of the flag rather than by estimation; `us_lab.o == 1` yields 11/18 but that is the US-lab geography share, not the lab share. Excluding the single `subjects.o == 'community'` study (id ee.4) would give 17/18.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Read data/meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv with NA tokens ('NA',''); verified shape (927,57) and project codes ml1/ml3/rpp/ee (ee = Experimental Economics, 18 rows). 2) Verified unit of analysis: ee rows are unique by id and by title (18/18/18, 0 dup O/R pairs), so row-level == unique-original-study-level. 3) Built denominator = ee rows with non-missing key marker `online.o` (NA=0 -> 18; NA never counted in denominator). 4) Applied PRIMARY definition `online.o == 0` plus sensitivity definitions (subjects.o pool restriction; subjects.o=='students' only; us_lab.o==1 labelled US-lab share, not lab share), reporting absolute counts next to every share. 5) Built marker-convergence table over `online.o`, `subjects.o`, `compensation.o`, `experiment_country.o` and checked the satisfied study SET is identical to the PRIMARY study set. 6) Crosstabbed PRIMARY x `subjects.o` and PRIMARY x `us_lab.o`. 7) Reported replication-side columns (`online.r`, `us_lab.r`, `subjects.r`) separately as transparency, never pooled. 8) Excluded the second CSV (replication_success) after verifying it has no setting columns. 9) Exported CSV/JSON artifacts and run log under work/out/. No ratio was computed before plan approval (skeleton ran in diagnostics-only mode).
